findings.current: But the Southern Heaven Demon Empress did not know that the young—almost absurdly young—enemy before her had once climbed a cliff with iron balls weighing well over a thousand *geun* strapped to his body.
findings.defect: The translation drops the preceding image that the pressure could crush a massive boulder in an instant.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly compares the pressure to a force that could crush a huge rock in one blow; the accepted baseline preserves this image.
findings.replacement: The pressure seemed capable of crushing even a massive boulder in an instant. But the Southern Heaven Demon Empress did not know that the young—almost absurdly young—enemy before her had once climbed a cliff with iron balls weighing well over a thousand *geun* strapped to his body.

findings.current: Fear that made every hair on his body stand on end seized Jin Taekyung.
findings.defect: The translation omits the comparison of the incoming force to a sea and a mountain rising and crashing down.
findings.rationale: The source uses both the sea-and-mountain image and the following fear reaction; the baseline preserves both.
findings.replacement: It was an overwhelming force, as though a sea and a mountain had risen and come crashing down upon him. Fear that made every hair on his body stand on end seized Jin Taekyung.

findings.current: People were born to forget, and the powerful, accustomed to causing pain, tended to forget their own.
findings.defect: The translation drops the source’s image of people as animals born to forget.
findings.rationale: The Korean calls people “animals of forgetfulness”; the accepted baseline preserves that image.
findings.replacement: Humans were animals born to forget, and the powerful, accustomed to causing pain, tended to forget their own.

summary: The assembled English has three minor source-image omissions.
